findings.risk: Weak, reused and never-rotated passwords are the primary credential-harvesting vector documented in all 5 Crimson Tide breaches (1x05).
findings.recommended_remediation: Deploy the 'MedDefense - Password and Lockout Policy' GPO enforcing 14-char minimum, complexity, and 24-password history.

findings.risk: No account lockout means unlimited password-spray and brute-force attempts against every one of the 14 domain accounts.
findings.recommended_remediation: Deploy the 'MedDefense - Password and Lockout Policy' GPO with a 5-attempt threshold and 15-minute lockout/reset window.

findings.evidence: Supported encryption types: DES, RC4, AES128, AES256
findings.risk: RC4/DES tickets are trivially crackable offline, enabling Kerberoasting and AS-REP roasting - the exact technique Crimson Tide Phase 3 (Lateral Movement) used for privilege escalation.
findings.recommended_remediation: Restrict 'Network security: Configure encryption types allowed for Kerberos' to AES128/AES256 only via GPO.
findings.mapped_task: pending: Kerberos encryption hardening task (not yet assigned)

findings.risk: Passwords that never expire never rotate - a single leaked credential from any of these accounts stays valid indefinitely.
findings.recommended_remediation: Clear PasswordNeverExpires on every non-service account; move required service-account exceptions under a managed service account (gMSA) or documented compensating control.
findings.mapped_task: pending: account lifecycle remediation task (not yet assigned)

findings.risk: A disabled account left in a privileged group is a re-enablement target - if the attacker resets its password (or it is re-enabled by mistake), it grants immediate domain-level access.
findings.recommended_remediation: Remove disabled accounts from all privileged groups; disabling an account does not revoke its group memberships.
findings.mapped_task: pending: privileged group cleanup task (not yet assigned)

findings.asset: Domain-wide audit policy and endpoint telemetry
findings.risk: Without process creation, account management and PowerShell logging, an attacker's actions after initial access generate zero evidence - exactly the blind spot Crimson Tide's affiliates relied on for lateral movement.
findings.recommended_remediation: Deploy the 'MedDefense - Advanced Audit Policy' GPO and roll out Sysmon with a detection-optimized configuration.

findings.risk: Unconstrained delegation lets any process that compromises this account impersonate ANY domain user to ANY service, including Domain Admins - the single fastest path from a compromised service account to full domain compromise.
findings.recommended_remediation: Convert every service account to constrained delegation (or resource-based constrained delegation); migrate to gMSA where possible.
findings.mapped_task: pending: service account hardening task (not yet assigned)

findings.risk: Stale computer objects are unmonitored, frequently unpatched, and are a common target for AD persistence (resource-based constrained delegation abuse, SPN spoofing).
findings.recommended_remediation: Disable and, after a grace period, remove computer objects with no authentication activity in 90+ days.
findings.mapped_task: pending: stale object cleanup task (not yet assigned)

findings.risk: Default-only GPOs mean nothing enforces password policy, audit policy, or endpoint restrictions domain-wide - and GPO itself is the exact mechanism Crimson Tide used to deploy ransomware to all 280 endpoints in Phase 6.
findings.recommended_remediation: Deploy MedDefense hardening GPOs (Tasks 4, 5 and beyond) and link them at the domain root or targeted OUs.
